title: Queen vs. Pawn
subtitle: Stop a pawn one step from promotion.
goals: Convert the frozen moments into king steps
Know the bishop-pawn and rook-pawn draws

steps.say: You won the pawn race and queened first — but the enemy pawn stands one step from its own coronation, and your king is far away. Queen versus pawn on the seventh: usually a win, but only with exact technique — and two famous pawns can hold a DRAW. Time to learn both sides.

steps.prompt: The queen can't stop the pawn from afar forever — your king must help. Start the winning machine: check, and force the king IN FRONT of his own pawn!
hints: The pawn only promotes when its king steps aside. Check him until he's forced onto e1 — blocking his own pawn — then your king gets a free step.
Qf5+ drives the king to the fatal square, then march: Kc5!

line.say: Check — and the king's only reasonable shelter is in front of his own pawn...
THE trick: with the king self-blocked on e1, the pawn is frozen — so this moment is a free step for YOUR king. Repeat the spiral: check, force the block, step closer.

rejections.say: e1=Q! You strolled while the pawn crowned — now it's a queen ending and the win is gone. The king may only approach during the FROZEN moments; force the block first with checks.
It eyes the pawn, but Kf1! and next the pawn promotes under escort — no check, no frozen moment, no time. Every move must force something.

steps.wrongSay: Check the king toward e1 — only when he blocks his own pawn do you earn a king step.
steps.successSay: Check, block, step — the spiral that reels your king in from anywhere on the board.

steps.prompt: The spiral continues: the king is blocked on e1 and yours is closing in. Play the full squeeze!
hints: The pawn is frozen while its king stands on e1 — take another free step, and be ready to re-check when he unblocks.
Kd4! If the king slips out to d1, pin the pawn from f1 and f2 — it can never promote while pinned to its king.

line.say: Another free step — and watch: Black's king has exactly ONE legal move...
Check! — covering the queening square at the same time...
The pin! The pawn is nailed to its king and can never promote — while your king strolls to e3 or d3 next move to end everything. The squeeze is complete.

rejections.say: Kxf1! The queen stepped adjacent to the king with no protection — check, capture, draw. She keeps her distance until your own king backs her up.
A step in the wrong rhythm — every approach must come during a frozen moment or with a concrete follow-up. Kd4 kept the king in the box.

steps.wrongSay: Free step now, then answer the unblock with checks and the f-file pin.
steps.successSay: Frozen king, pinned pawn, marching monarch — the complete winning method against a center pawn.

steps.prompt: Your king has arrived. Finish with precision — one natural-looking move throws the win away!
hints: Careful: the pawn is defended by its king. Look for the quiet move that ends everything at once.
Qg1 — check on the back rank while your king covers d1 and d2. Count every escape.

line.say: Checkmate! The back-rank check meets your king's coverage of d1 and d2 — the pawn never got to be anything but a bystander. Technique to the very last move.

rejections.say: Kxe2!! The pawn was defended by its king — you just handed back the queen and the game is a draw. At the finish line, greed is fatal: the quiet Qg1 was mate.

steps.wrongSay: Not the pawn — the KING. One queen move mates immediately.
steps.successSay: Won with a mate, not a grab. The last move of good technique is always the safest one.

steps.say: Now the exception every strong player knows: the BISHOP PAWN (c- or f-file). Watch Black's fiendish defense — White's queen attacks the pawn, and Black...

autoMoves.say: ...dives into the corner! Now Qxc2 is STALEMATE — a2, b1 and b2 are all covered, but there's no check. And any other try lets the pawn keep threatening to queen. With White's king this far away: DRAW. The same trick works for rook pawns (a/h) — but never for center or knight pawns. Know your exceptions!
